messages:
alex_chen: quick heads-up — ran a latency sweep for a newly onboarded quantized model (llama3-small-int8) across H100/A100 in us-east, us-west, eu-west. p50s are fine but p95 in eu-west is high (seen ~420ms on H100). suspect edge routing/proxy egress causing extra hop.

alex_chen: short summary (seq=64, batch=1, steady-state after 2k warmups, 10k requests):
H100 us-east: 110 / 240 ms
H100 us-west: 130 / 260 ms
H100 eu-west: 160 / 420 ms
A100 us-east: 140 / 300 ms
A100 eu-west: 180 / 510 ms

maria_garcia: can you share the exact request you used + headers? did you force any regional routing header?

alex_chen: yep — used the test harness with an override header to exercise edge variants. command:```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" \n     -H "X-Edge-Route: prefer-direct" \n     -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west" \n     -d '{"input":"ping"}' \n     https://api.staging.redwood/serve/llama3-small-int8/generate
```
(The header 'X-Edge-Route' toggles which edge proxy pool the request prefers in the test infra)

sanjay_patel: did you capture kernel selection logs on the serving host? if eu-west hosts fell back to a slower kernel that could explain the tail. also cold vs warm kv-cache?

alex_chen: kernel selection snippet from logs (eu-west host):
```
[2026-03-19T14:12:03Z] model=llama3-small-int8 device=h100 kernel=fused_attention_v2 status=ok
[2026-03-19T14:12:03Z] model=llama3-small-int8 device=h100 kernel=fallback_attention status=warn reason=missing-vectorized-kernel
```
So the orchestration tried fused_attention_v2 but some hosts fell back to fallback_attention (non-vectorized) — likely due to a driver/kernel mismatch on a subset of eu-west nodes. kv-cache: we warmed for 2k requests before sampling.

jen_lopez: can you run a bypass test that hits the origin inference pool directly (bypass proxy) to confirm routing delta? also traceroute from the proxy egress to the inference node to see extra hops.

alex_chen: ran a direct origin run and a proxy run back-to-back. results:
- via proxy (normal): H100 eu-west p95 = 420ms
- direct origin (bypassed proxy): H100 eu-west p95 = 230ms
So bypassing proxy cuts the tail in half.

alex_chen: sample traceroute from eu-west proxy to inference node:
```
1  10.0.0.1  0.6 ms
2  10.0.5.3  1.2 ms
3  100.120.8.2  12.8 ms  <-- transit gateway
4  100.120.9.5  14.0 ms
5  10.200.3.7  15.1 ms  <-- inference host
```
There are two extra network hops and a transit gateway that adds jitter.

maria_garcia: interesting. could be a mix of (1) kernel fallback on some eu-west hosts and (2) extra proxy transit jitter. both can explain the p95 inflation.

infra-bot: FYI — eu-west h100 pool currently has 2 hosts on driver vX.Y (known issue) flagged for kernel incompatibility. ticket #INF-4521.

deploy-bot: canary: rerouting 15% of eu-west traffic to alt-edge pool to test lower-hop path.

alex_chen: rerun after canary (15%): eu-west p95 for H100 dropped to ~310ms — improvement but still above us-east. indicates kernel mismatch still contributes. after we patch drivers on the 2 hosts I expect parity.

sanjay_patel: action list: (1) patch eu-west hosts in INF-4521 (drivers/kernels) (2) instrument edge proxy hop count and add metric to per-route dashboard (3) run a targeted kernel-only A/B (force kernel selection) to measure pure kernel impact.

jen_lopez: I'll add traceroute-based hop histogram to the console dashboards and annotate the eu-west route.

alex_chen: I also saved the raw bench CSVs and a small reproducer script. if anyone wants the harness I'll drop it in #eng-ml-artifacts. thanks — leaning to label this as a combined routing+kernel tail regression rather than a model quant issue. :white_check_mark:
